ai_summary: Great Britain’s electricity system is currently operating with total wind output at 8.3 GW, of which Scottish wind contributes an estimated 1.8 GW, representing 17.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Generation within Scotland delivers a carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the GB-wide carbon intensity of 172 gCO2/kWh. Transmission bottlenecks continue to impede the delivery of this clean generation to southern demand centers. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today stands at 578 MWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £38,660. To balance the system and replace this curtailed zero-carbon volume, fossil generation elsewhere required an estimated 109,820 m3 of gas to be burned, emitting an additional 202 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing today’s constraint expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £14 million. In terms of consumer impact, while this intervention equates to an immediate system balancing cost of roughly £67 per curtailed MWh, calculating the precise £/MWh increase across every consumer's invoice in the UK cannot be completed without introducing external total national demand figures, strictly adhering to the provided data constraints.
